name: LSASS Memory
why: Attacker reads LSASS process memory to steal cached credentials and NTLM hashes. This is a critical credential access vector used in 80%+ of breach campaigns.
satisfied_requirements: EDR: LSASS Protection (Credential Guard / ASR rule)

name: SAM Registry
why: Attacker accesses SAM (Security Account Manager) registry hive to extract local account hashes. This is common in lateral movement after initial access.
satisfied_requirements: Windows Event Log: Registry Access Audit (Event 4663)
SIEM: Alert rule on SAM registry access

name: DCSync
why: Attacker uses Directory Replication Service to request password hashes from domain controller. No credentials needed — only user rights (often obtained via compromised admin account).
satisfied_requirements: Windows Event Log: Active Directory Replication Events (4662, 4663, 4662)
SIEM: Alert rule on unusual replication requests

name: PowerShell Execution
why: PowerShell is the primary execution vector for post-exploitation. Most C2 frameworks, credential dumping tools, and lateral movement use PowerShell.
satisfied_requirements: Windows Event Log: PowerShell Script Block Logging (Event 4104)
SIEM: Alert rule on suspicious PowerShell flags

name: DNS (C2 / Exfiltration)
why: DNS is rarely inspected but is a common covert channel for C2 beaconing and data exfiltration. Attackers encode commands in DNS queries → hard to detect without baseline.

name: Scheduled Task Creation
why: Scheduled tasks are low-noise persistence mechanism. After initial access, attacker creates task to re-establish access on reboot/cleanup.
satisfied_requirements: Windows Event Log: Task Scheduler Creation (Event 4698, 4699)
SIEM: Alert rule on task creation

name: Disable or Modify Tools
why: Disabling AV/EDR is the first step of any breach. This is the highest-value alert in the kill chain.
